ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10619 of 28 April 2011, as amended), especially Articles 2, 5-2, 6 and 11; Enforcement Decree of the Same Act; Criminal Proceeds Concealment Regulation Act (Act No. 10627, as amended); Act on the Prohibition of Financing of Offenses against Public Peace (Act No. 10628, as amended); Financial Services Commission Notifications and KoFIU Guidance on Customer Due Diligence and Identification of Beneficial Owners; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 13070, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree regulating licensed cross-border remittance agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Corporate Registration Certificate, Beop-in Deung-gi Sa-hang Jeung-myeong)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea District Registry Court (Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive authentication path selected solely by the receiving state: if the receiving state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, attach a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille only; if the receiving state is not an Apostille Convention member, use only consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction in the destination state; never combine or sequence apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Tax Payment and No Tax Delinquency (Guk-se Nae-gye Jeung-myeong)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the competent district tax office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the destination jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, authenticate the document exclusively through a Hague apostille issued by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs; if the destination jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member, authenticate exclusively through consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate of the destination country. These routes are mutually exclusive and never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Pre-Incorporation, Registered Office Execution and Regulatory Filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization at the Korean notary office, then either (i) Hague apostille by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention receiving jurisdictions, or (ii) consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate for non-member receiving jurisdictions. Only the route required by the destination is used; apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must not be applied to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeong-gwan) for Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and certified Korean Notary Public; duly filed with the district registry court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: After notarization, authenticate for foreign use exclusively by the Hague apostille process through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs when the receiving state is a member of the Apostille Convention, or exclusively by consular legalization through the Korean Embassy or Consulate when the receiving state is a non-member. No document receives both forms of authentication sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Bank Reference Letter / Financial Institution Due Diligence Letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank holding the applicant's or principal's verified corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the Korean bank and authenticated through one of two parallel routes: Hague apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention destination jurisdictions, or consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction for non-Apostille destinations. The route is selected based on destination membership, with no sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening requires the remittance agent to identify and verify all beneficial owners, authorized signatories, counterparties, and correspondent banks against: (i) domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates as defined by KoFIU guidance and FATF Recommendation 12; (ii) United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, including all consolidated UN designations; (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, Sectoral Sanctions, and the 50 percent rule; (iv) U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security Entity List; (v) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions; and (vi) Korean domestic designations and asset freeze orders under the Act on the Prohibition of Financing of Offenses against Public Peace. Screening must be real-time at onboarding, continuously refreshed, and repeated on every transaction, with automatic escalation, enhanced due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting to KoFIU, and comprehensive audit trail retention under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO), available at www.iros.go.kr, together with the commercial registration information system operating under the Supreme Court Registration Office for same and similar trade name searches
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and registration practice, the legal entity name must be expressed in Korean (Hangul) and must include 'Yuhan Hoesa' as the mandatory corporate form suffix indicating a limited liability company. A corresponding English or foreign-language trade name may be separately registered, but the Korean name must be a faithful phonetic transliteration that does not collide with existing registered names. The four-tier naming convention consists of: (i) the foreign-language trade name, (ii) the Hangul transliteration, (iii) the business-purpose descriptive elements, and (iv) the 'Yuhan Hoesa' entity-type suffix. Names with Hanja or other script may be used only as descriptive parentheticals, never as the primary statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days from written rejection by the registration officer, file a registration objection with the district court having jurisdiction over the registry, stating each rejected name element and proposing a compliant alternative. If the objection is dismissed, file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Civil Procedure Rules with the appellate court within 14 days, and thereafter a Supreme Court final appeal where the appellate decision conflicts with precedent. Parallel remedy: amend the proposed name and resubmit a fresh incorporation application through the Internet Registration Office. The appeal right is independent of resubmission and should be exercised promptly to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial-mailbox-only arrangement is not permissible for a Yuhan Hoesa conducting cross-border remittance services. The Financial Services Commission, KoFIU, Korea Customs Service, and National Tax Service require a fixed physical place of business in Korea with a compliance officer or responsible manager, complete books and records, physical AML transaction-monitoring infrastructure, and accessible customer due diligence files. National Tax Service registration presumes fixed business premises; a P.O. Box or virtual address triggers mandatory enhanced inspection and constitutes grounds for refusal of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act registration or a bank account relationship. For this high-risk special-license industry, virtual offices are categorically rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) valid lease agreement identifying a real, fixed premises with Korean signage; (2) full-time staff physically present during business hours; (3) original AML manual, transaction monitoring logs, client files and board minutes maintained on site; (4) dedicated servers, computer terminals and CCTV or security arrangements consistent with bank and Korea Customs Service expectations; (5) no virtual mailbox, sub-post office box, or forwarding-only address. Quantified risk: high, approximately 75-90 percent risk of an unannounced on-site inspection by the National Tax Service, local municipal tax authorities, Financial Supervisory Service, KoFIU, or Korea Customs Service within the first 12 months of operation for a licensed cross-border remittance entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (상법), Act No. 1000, as amended, particularly Articles 287-1 through 287-74 (Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa); also the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (외국환거래법) and Electronic Financial Transactions Act (전자금융거래법) for licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Registry Office (법원등기국) via local district court registry (지방법원등기과) with jurisdiction over the company's registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Application for Company Registration (회사설립등기신청서) filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the company must have a paid-in capital sufficient to cover its business operations, and for remittance services, the Financial Services Commission may require a minimum capital of KRW 1 billion (approx. USD 750,000) under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. This capital must be deposited in a domestic bank account and remain unencumbered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing and registration are conducted through the Home Tax Service (Hometax) internet portal at www.hometax.go.kr. Customs-related export declarations are handled through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) maintaining a registered Korean place of business must obtain a Business Registration Certificate (BRC), which contains the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) serving as both the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the VAT identification number. Procedure: (1) complete incorporation and court registration under the Korean Commercial Act at the local district court registry; (2) file a business registration application with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the head office within twenty days of business commencement, either through the Hometax electronic portal or by in-person submission; (3) submit the prescribed application form, court registration certificate, articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, proof of the Korean place of business (lease or ownership), shareholder registry, and a power of attorney appointing a domestic tax representative where non-resident shareholders are involved; (4) receive the BRC with the BRN from the NTS; (5) in addition, foreign non-resident shareholders without a Korean domestic presence must provide evidence of their foreign registration details and may be issued a separate non-resident corporate code for withholding tax documentation purposes. The BRN must be quoted on all tax invoices, customs declarations, and VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not offer a check-the-box or comparable entity-classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a resident corporation under the Corporate Tax Act, taxable at the entity level on worldwide income, with no pass-through to shareholders. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied under the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework, but no elective classification regime exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) imposed under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW — No statutory turnover threshold. Any person including a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in a taxable business activity in South Korea is required to register with the National Tax Service within twenty days of business commencement. Small business persons may file a simplified VAT return, but registration remains mandatory from the date of commencement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices issued by a registered business in South Korea must be issued as electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice / Jeonja Segaese-gyesan) and transmitted to the National Tax Service via the Home Tax Service (Hometax) portal or through an NTS-accredited electronic invoice service provider. Transmission is mandatory on or before the day following the date of invoice issuance (T+1). There is no pre-issuance fiscal clearance or physical anti-fraud stamping regime; integrity is secured through the NTS electronic tax invoice management system using unique invoice numbers, digital authentication, and real-time e-invoice data matching. API-based integration is permitted for licensed e-invoice providers using the NTS XML interface.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Articles 21 and 24 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act for the export of goods that are physically moved outside Korea under an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, and for the supply of services to a non-resident or foreign enterprise where the service is deemed to be provided in a foreign territory, the recipient is outside Korea, and the consideration is received in convertible foreign currency or through an internationally recognized settlement mechanism. In the context of the cross-border remittance platform, service fees charged to expatriate workers located outside Korea for the use of money-transmission rails may qualify as zero-rated exported services when the recipient is a non-resident, the service is performed from Korea through SWIFT or local cash-pickup clearing networks, and the fee is paid to the Korean entity's foreign-currency account. Supplies to Korean residents or services not meeting the foreign-currency and non-resident-usage tests remain subject to VAT at the standard rate of 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Declaration accepted through the UNI-PASS portal)
Bill of Lading (Ocean) or Air Waybill (Air) as applicable to the physical export of goods
Commercial Invoice and Sales Contract / Service Agreement clearly identifying the foreign buyer or non-resident recipient and the nature of the cross-border service

Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation (Foreign Remittance Certificate / Foreign Currency Receipt Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank, evidencing inward remittance and repatriation of the export or service proceeds)
Electronic Tax Invoice issuance and transmission record from the Hometax VAT system, retained with the VAT export-ledger for audit inspection
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and VAT refund claims are subject to documentary audit by the National Tax Service and the Korea Customs Service. If the export or foreign-currency settlement documentation cannot be substantiated within the statutory review period, the NTS will reassess the VAT at 10% on the supply value, impose statutory additional taxes for false or unsupported tax invoices, and charge interest from the original due date. Fraudulent or repeated zero-rating claims may be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying criminal penalties of imprisonment up to five years and/or fines up to KRW 50 million. Unlawfully obtained VAT refunds are subject to retrospective clawback with prescribed interest and penalty surcharges, and the statutory limitation period for tax reassessment is generally five years from the taxable date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), functioning as the central bank in cooperation with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the authorized foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) for the administration, surveillance, and enforcement of the Korean foreign exchange control system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalized yet declaratory foreign exchange regime. Current-account transactions, including trade settlements, service fees, dividends, interest, and generally recurring business payments, are freely convertible for resident companies and non-resident investors within the scope of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital-account transactions are permissible but require prior reporting, registration, or execution through an authorized foreign exchange bank for categories such as foreign direct investment, cross-border financing, and acquisition of securities. There is no general forced surrender for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in licensed domestic foreign currency accounts after collection, but every transaction must be routed through and declared to an authorized foreign exchange bank. Profit remittances are processed without central bank pre-approval once the bank verifies the audited financial statements, the tax withholding certificates, and the board resolution approving the dividend. The practical convertibility experience is efficient for current-account items, while capital-account items demand strict documentary discipline to avoid the reactive controls or administrative penalties that FETA can impose for unreported or mischaracterized transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect foreign currency export and service proceeds within one year from the date of export declaration or from the completion date of the exported service, unless the Ministry of Economy and Finance grants an extension under FETA. Upon collection, the exporter must deposit the full amount in a domestic foreign currency account with an authorized foreign exchange bank or sell the proceeds to that bank; the mandatory conversion ratio is zero because 100 percent may be retained in foreign currency, but the funds must flow through an authorized foreign exchange bank and be reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Operational Account and Foreign Currency Escrow Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and Capital Contribution Escrow Account
General Corporate Sweep Account and Foreign Currency Money Transmission Clearing Account
Trade Settlement Account and Domestic Wired Transfer Concentration Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. A non-resident offshore digital EMI, including a fully authorized European electronic money institution, cannot independently offer Korean won clearing, local cash pickup, or direct settlement services in Korea without becoming an authorized foreign exchange bank or entering into a regulated agency or technical-services relationship with a domestic branch-based licensed bank. FETA requires any entity engaged in cross-border money transmission in Korea to hold a recognized foreign exchange business registration or an equivalent payment service provider license. Offshore EMIs may act only as a customer-facing orchestration layer, compliance-reporting intermediary, or data processor, while all actual clearing and settlement must be executed through domestic Tier-1 commercial banks. The fixed viability of a pure fintech EMI route is therefore rated low, with legal and regulatory risk rated high.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a high-risk remittance license holder, the statutory director and the designated AML compliance officer of Yuhan Hoesa must appear physically in-branch before the corporate banking relationship manager. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted by Tier-1 Korean banks for this business type. For non-resident co-signatories or foreign directors not travelling to Korea, a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, combined with a video conference interview and onshore Korean legal counsel attendance, may be used to complete the mandate, provided that at least one statutory director with ultimate signature authority appears in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution from a non-resident shareholder lacks an independently verifiable source-of-wealth trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a twelve-month bank statement from the remitting shareholder or corporate parent, certified tax returns audited by an internationally recognized accounting firm, a signed shareholder biography describing the current business and wealth creation, confirmation of the specific source of funds for the contribution, and a completed adverse media and sanctions screening report for the beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership cannot be conclusively determined due to a multi-tiered foreign shareholding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a full corporate chain diagram showing every intermediate entity, certified copies of certificates of incorporation and share registers for each entity in the chain, passport copies of all natural persons owning more than 25 percent, and a notarized beneficial ownership declaration stating that no nominee shares or undisclosed trusts exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6619 money transmission activity represents an inherently high-risk sector for unlawful cross-border remittance and trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the special remittance license issued or recognized by the Financial Services Commission, a comprehensive AML/CFT manual aligned with Financial Action Task Force standards, the transaction-monitoring system specification, a board-approved customer risk acceptance policy for cash pickup corridors, and proof of appointment of a resident AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential failure to report foreign-exchange transactions could expose both the bank and the entity to FETA criminal and civil liability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the FETA registration certificate for foreign exchange business, an executed undertaking to route all transactions through authorized foreign exchange banks, a transaction reporting workflow covering the Foreign Exchange Information System, and a written compliance opinion from a Korean law firm confirming all reporting responsibilities and the fit of the proposed clearing rails.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent shall remit the KRW or USD capital contribution via a SWIFT MT103 message into Yuhan Hoesa's capital contribution escrow account at one of the Tier-1 domestic banks. The MT103 must carry the foreign exchange purpose code for inward direct investment, such as acquisition of an equity interest in a Korean company, and the remitter name must exactly match the registered foreign investor. The beneficiary bank will verify that the prior foreign direct investment notification has been correctly filed through the Foreign Investment Support Center or the designated foreign exchange bank, and will hold the funds until the auditor or certified public accountant issues the capital verification certificate for the Korean court registration file. The same escrow rail remains available for subsequent paid-in capital increases and must be mirrored in the company's statutory registered capital records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for the remittance business should be settled through SWIFT MT103 messages for correspondent banking transfers, Korean won domestic disbursements through BOK-Wire or the domestic electronic clearing system, and international trade settlements through commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600 or documentary collections governed by URC522 when the underlying transaction is a sale of goods. For consumer remittance payouts, the preferred clearing rail is real-time domestic cash pickup through the partner Korean bank's branch network, supported by ACH transfers where cash pickup is not available. All outbound transactions must be reconciled daily against the Foreign Exchange Information System reporting files, with monthly reconciliation against the bank statements maintained for the supervisory authority.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW foreign exchange forward contracts against a demonstrable trade or transaction exposure through an authorized foreign exchange bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the Korean entity or the offshore parent where the underlying exposure is a cross-border remittance business receivable
Cross-currency swaps for long-term funding linked to underlying foreign currency debt and confirmed future remittance cash flows
Plain-vanilla foreign exchange options and rolling FX swaps with a licensed Korean bank, subject to the bank's credit line and verification of the underlying commercial transaction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the local district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal-year end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; false or fraudulent reporting attracts a negligence tax up to 40%; daily delinquency surcharge accrues until payment; prolonged non-filing triggers tax seizure, restriction of the remittance licence, and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the national corporate income tax return, being by March 31 of the following year for a calendar-year entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A monthly local surcharge of 0.75% on unpaid local corporate tax; repeated non-payment can lead to forced collection and cancellation of business-related local licences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and External Auditor Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART e-disclosure system; the external audit report is also filed at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six weeks after the external auditor issues the report, and in no event later than the extended statutory audit filing deadline of April 30 following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to file the audited financial statements is punished under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies with criminal fines up to KRW 50,000,000; administrative orders and auditor disqualification can follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Foreign Exchange Transaction Division, with interface to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 for the calendar-year licence period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 50,000,000; late filing can lead to ordering of business suspension and, on repeated violation, revocation of the foreign exchange remittance licence under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT and Beneficial Ownership Control Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 of the following year for the prior calendar year AML compliance data; suspicious transaction reports and cash transaction reports must be filed continuously on a real-time basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or file AML records triggers administrative fines under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, plus supervisory sanctions against the registered remittance operator; wilful violations expose officers to imprisonment up to five years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified CPA audit is mandatory under the Korean External Audit Act when: (i) total assets at the end of the preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000, approximately USD 9,200,000; (ii) the entity is a stock company listed on the Korea Exchange; (iii) the entity is a licensed financial or remittance business designated by the Financial Services Commission as requiring public disclosure or audited statements regardless of asset size; or (iv) the entity is otherwise selected by the regulator for audit due to public-interest designation. South Korea does not use turnover or employee count as independent statutory audit triggers for a Yuhan Hoesa; the decisive quantitative test is the balance-sheet total asset threshold plus the financial-licence character of the business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Licensed cross-border remittance operators must apply Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). If the Yuhan Hoesa does not exceed K-IFRS mandatory application thresholds and is not a financial licence-holder, it may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP); there is no separate SME financial reporting standard requiring exemption from full K-GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require an annual UBO confirmation return for a private Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, the remittance licence imposes a continuous beneficial-ownership compliance obligation under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information. The licensee must maintain an internal record of the true controlling members, senior managing agents, and beneficial owners; update the record within 30 days after any shareholding transfer, ownership change, or change of managing members; notify the Financial Supervisory Service of material ownership changes as a condition of the foreign exchange licence; and report suspicious transactions to KoFIU immediately if unexplained controllers are identified. Any change in directors or representative members must also be registered at the District Court Commercial Registration Bureau within 14 days under the Korean Commercial Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (member qualification ledger) kept at the registered office for the Yuhan Hoesa
Register of Directors and Managing Members
Minutes of General Members Meetings and Board Resolutions
Accounting books and vouchers, including bank statements and customer remittance transaction ledgers
Register of Charges or Mortgages over company assets and any collateral assignments supporting the cross-border clearing arrangements
AML customer due diligence files and suspicious transaction log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 to USD 30,000 per certified audit engagement depending on transaction volume and cross-border settlement complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; lower brackets apply: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion. An additional 10% local income surtax is imposed on national tax payable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean Tax Incentives: foreign-invested high-tech businesses in Free Economic Zones may qualify for 100%/50% corporate tax reductions for 5/3 years; R&D expenses are eligible for 20%-50% incremental tax deductions or 2% current-year additional deductions; facility investments and job-creating investments are available under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; technology transfer income may be eligible for a 50% corporate tax exemption under Article 12 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Domestic corporate income tax return: Comprehensive Corporate Tax Standard Return (법인사업자 종합법인세 신고서) filed through HomeTax (hometax.go.kr), the National Tax Service electronic filing portal. A foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa must also attach the non-resident shareholder report and any DTA relief application using Form 23 (Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return and tax payment are due within three months from the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following year. If the accounting period ends on another date, the deadline is within three months after that accounting closing date. A one-month extension is available when the financial statements are audited under the External Audit Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 (Financial Statement Summary / Profit and Loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total revenue, gross income, cost of services, operating expenses, and net income for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa. For cross-border remittance rails, revenue consists of transaction fees, FX spreads, convenience charges, and settlement interest; commission expense is deductible only if actually paid to the licensed remittance aggregator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net foreign exchange gains against operating revenue unless permitted under K-IFRS; all income derived from the Korean remittance platform is Korean-source. Foreign remittance software fees paid to a non-resident licensor are royalties subject to withholding at the statutory rate unless the rate is reduced under the relevant bilateral tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Schedule of Adjustments to Taxable Income: Additions and Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile book net income to corporate taxable income by adding non-deductible reserves, donations, excessive entertainment costs, and non-deductible internal service charges; subtract non-taxable dividends, tax-exempt technology transfer gains, and deductible reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border remittance operations, ancillary expenses invoiced by overseas group companies are tested against the arm's length standard. Excessive management fees paid to a non-resident parent may be reclassified as constructive dividends and assessed with a 15% penalty surcharge when no economic substance in the intercompany agreement is established.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Tax Base Computations and Tax Credit Section)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate progressive national corporate income tax and the 10% local surtax on the national income tax liability; claim foreign tax credits for withholding taxes suffered in other jurisdictions and apply qualifying investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa taxed at entity level cannot flow through foreign income to non-resident shareholders. The LLC must separately file the Foreign Tax Credit Schedule; if DTA relief on outbound remittances is expected, the withholding declaration in Box 6 must contain a reconciled beneficial owner list supported by Tax Residency Certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Statement of International Related Transactions / Transfer Pricing Attachment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report each international related-party transaction by counterparty, country, transaction type, transfer pricing method, margin, and any advance pricing agreement. Attach Master File, Local File, and Country-by-Country Report when the statutory thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A remittance routed through a Hong Kong settlement affiliate must use either a Comparable Uncontrolled Price test for the USD spread charged or the Transactional Net Margin Method benchmarked against Korean remittance agencies. The transfer pricing schedule must be filed through HomeTax within the filing deadline, including intercompany loan interest payable to the foreign treasury entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Non-Resident Investor Ownership and Treaty Declaration Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose the name, country of residence, ownership ratio, share capital contribution, and acquisition date of every non-resident shareholder, including each ultimate beneficial owner; confirm whether the foreign investor has applied for reduced treaty withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the immediate shareholder is a zero-employee licensed entity with no office in its claimed jurisdiction, the Korean tax authorities may deny treaty relief because the beneficial ownership requirement is not satisfied. Reduced DTA rates are unavailable when the shareholder is an agent, nominee, or conduit. A Korea-based remittance service must maintain an updated ownership chart and proof of actual commercial activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Withholding Remittance Report for Dividends, Interest, and Royalties)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report Korean-source dividends, interest, royalties, and other consideration paid to non-resident recipients before the prescribed withholding periods, identify the DTA article and rate, calculate withholding at the statutory 20% national rate plus 2% local income surtax, and claim treaty rate reductions using Form 23.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remittance outflows paid through SWIFT or local cash pickup are taxable when credited to the non-resident beneficiary. No cost deduction is allowed against the gross amount before withholding. The return must distinguish settlement-only flows from taxable income and confirm the same-state beneficial owner status. A failure to file this box may expose the company to a deemed-dividend adjustment and criminal penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without reasonable cause attracts an additional tax of 0.3% of the unpaid tax for each day of delay, capped at 75% of the unpaid tax, plus a 20% negligence surcharge; fraudulent or unjustified returns attract a 40% penalty surcharge under the Basic Act for National Taxes. Failure to file the non-resident dividend withholding return exposes a manager to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million and further penalty tax. Criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can result in imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of up to three times the evaded amount; directors may also be blacklisted and detained following a travel ban while the seizure is pending.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income surtax on the national tax, resulting in an effective statutory 22% withholding on outbound dividends paid by a Yuhan Hoesa to non-resident shareholders when no treaty relief applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA withholding: 1) obtain the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the home tax authority for the current calendar year; 2) submit Form 23 (Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction) with the withholding return through HomeTax or to the competent district tax office; 3) attach the relevant contract, payment invoice, corporate registration certificates, and an ownership chart proving the recipient is the beneficial owner with full rights to receive and dispose of the income; 4) retain the TRC and supporting evidence for at least five years; 5) if tax was withheld at 22% and treaty relief should have applied, file a corrective withholding return and apply for a refund through the Seoul National Tax Service within the statutory refund period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Korean-source royalty and interest paid to non-residents are subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local income surtax for an effective 22% rate. Treaty rates vary: for example, Korea-US interest may be reduced to 10% and royalties to 10% for a beneficial owner entitled to the treaty; Korea-UK royalties and interest are generally reduced to 10%; Korea-China royalties and interest are generally reduced to 10%. Treaty relief is conditional on beneficial ownership, absence of a Korean permanent establishment, and the filing of Form 23.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, a Korean entity must prepare and submit a Master File and Local File when the aggregate volume of international related-party transactions exceeds KRW 50 billion in the preceding business year. A Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for a Korea-resident constituent entity of a multinational group whose consolidated revenue is at least KRW 100 billion in the preceding fiscal year. Even below the threshold, cross-border remittance fee arrangements must be supported by an arm's length benchmark study.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Korean tax authorities apply the substance-over-form doctrine and the General Anti-Abuse Rule under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17. Cross-border remittance income will be recharacterized where the Korean entity lacks Core Income-Generating Activities such as employees, contracts, risk management, settlement operations, and licensing. A Yuhan Hoesa that is only a booking center with no operational substance will be treated as a conduit, the income may be attributed to the overseas principal, and a permanent establishment of the foreign enterprise may be found under the DTA and Korean domestic PE rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting remittance volume and FX income, filing false HomeTax statements, or mischaracterizing shareholder dividends as technical service fees with no valid contract and no withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 imposes imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding three times the grossly evaded tax. The Corporate Tax Act applies a 40% penalty surcharge for fraudulent filing and a 20% penalty for negligent filing. The National Tax Service may also revoke licenses under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act in connection with unregistered remittance activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the director used the Yuhan Hoesa as an alter ego, personally ordered the concealment, or stripped the company of assets. The director is jointly and severally liable for corporate tax, interest, and penalties; the National Tax Service may impose a travel ban, blacklist the director, seize personal bank accounts and real property, and obtain civil restitution by provisional attachment and execution. The director may serve up to 5 years of imprisonment and pay a fine equal to three times the evaded amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Treaty Benefits in Remittance Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a zero-employee Hong Kong, Singapore, or BVI intermediary between the Korean remittance entity and the foreign beneficiary, with no real management, no office, no binding commercial contract, and no Korean AML reporting, solely to access a lower DTA rate or to defer withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean tax courts apply substance-over-form and the OECD BEPS principle to deny treaty benefits. The National Tax Service will reclassify the intermediary's income as Korean-source, apply the 22% statutory withholding instead of the claimed 10% treaty rate, impose the 40% fraudulent-return penalty, and refer the matter to the prosecution service under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information. The shell will be blacklisted for foreign exchange settlement and the remittance license may be cancelled by the Financial Services Commission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the shell invoice or established the conduit as a nominee are jointly liable for unpaid corporate tax and interest. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 23 permits administrative fines and penal detention for directors who allow an unreported cross-border remittance through a shell. Personal accounts are frozen by the Financial Intelligence Unit during the AML blacklist period; the director faces up to 3 years of imprisonment for participating in an unauthorized remittance business and civil asset restitution for fraudulent transfers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Violation / Unlicensed Cross-Border Money Transmission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commencing remittance services before obtaining the statutory payment institution license, failing to file suspicious transaction reports, failing to identify the beneficial owner of each remittance, or structuring SWIFT cash pickup payments to avoid the KRW 10 million transaction reporting threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unauthorized money transmission is a criminal offense under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. The Financial Services Commission may impose an administrative fine of up to KRW 100 million, and organized habitual violations subject directors to aggravated punishment under the Act on the Punishment of Specific Financial Crimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced against directors who controlled the remittance platform: each director faces up to 5 years of actual imprisonment, a KRW 50 million fine, confiscation of illegal commissions, civil asset restitution to harmed customers, and a travel ban. The director may be barred from financial institution management for up to 5 years. The Financial Intelligence Unit can enforce asset freezing against the director's personal bank accounts and real property for up to four days or longer during prosecution.
